key_insight: Chemical disorder in high-entropy ceramics creates a quantum vibrational stabilization mechanism—via phonon spectral broadening—that can offset unfavorable mixing enthalpy and suppress phase separation.
engineering_relevance: The framework enables million-scale, DFT-accurate screening of multicomponent ceramics, helping engineers identify compositions that balance high-temperature stiffness, low thermal conductivity, and phase stability.
method: Quantum spectral thermodynamics links phonon self-energy/broadening to free energy.
Uncertainty-guided active learning explores compositional space at DFT fidelity.
Million-scale search across 7.7 million ceramic configurations accelerates discovery by ~10^5×.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports screening 7.7 million high-entropy ceramic configurations and finding an approximately 12 at.% solute threshold separating strengthening from softening behavior.
watch_item: The active-learning predictions and stabilization trends should still be validated experimentally for specific chemistries and processing conditions, since real materials may deviate from idealized DFT-based models.
paper_title: Quantum spectral thermodynamics and active learning enable million-scale exploration of high-entropy ceramics
